transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Nora (Redwood CSM); Jordan (SunForge), Priya (SunForge), Liam (SunForge CTO)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion readout. SunForge wants a 20% capacity top-up, add EU AZ region (eu-west-az), discuss latency SLAs, KMS integration and contract amendment timeline. Agreed to run a short benchmark and share security docs.

Topics:
- Current usage & burst patterns
- Dedicated vs hosted capacity for predictable latency
- VPC/KMS and SOC2 requirements
- Pricing tiers and PO timing

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, quick check-in to run through the top-up plan and EU roll out readout.
[00:14] Jordan Beck: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we ran the traffic sim last week, saw spikes around midday hitting 16k tokens/min with p99 latency creeping up, so want to add headroom.
[00:29] Carlos Ortiz: got it. the 16k tokens/min — that's across both hosted and dedicated usage?
[00:36] Priya Singh: primarily hosted now, we allocated a small dedicated pool for inference experiments but most prod is via the hosted endpoints.
[00:45] Carlos Ortiz: ok that makes sense. for predictable p99 we usually recommend dedicated capacity with the burst cushion — gives you deterministic throughput. but that comes with commit terms.
[01:02] Liam O'Neill: quick question on latency tradeoffs — if we go dedicated, can we keep the same model variants and quantization profiles? We tested 4-bit in staging and quality was okay but we worry about regressions.
[01:16] Carlos Ortiz: yes, you can pin model versions. quantization and runtime kernels are configurable — we'll snapshot profiles. we'll also run the benchmark you're asking for using your prompt set so we can verify quality/latency tradeoffs.
[01:33] Jordan Beck: perfect. about regions — we need eu-west-az for data residency and reduce p99 for EU customers. curious about deployment lead time and whether it's a private VPC or hosted in our tenant.
[01:48] Maya Patel: deployment options: for eu region we can provision hosted capacity inside our EU cluster (fastest) or set up Dedicated in that region with VPC peering. if you need customer-managed network and KMS, that's the Private path and typically takes longer (2–4 weeks extra) for networking + KMS.
[02:08] Priya Singh: we definitely need KMS and SSO integration — compliance requires CMK. SOC2 is already in your docs right?
[02:16] Nora Kim: yes we'll share the SOC 2 pack and a network diagram. KMS integration details are in the private deploy checklist, we'll include sample terraform for KMS grants.
[02:28] Liam O'Neill: and what's the fallback if eu capacity is constrained? we can't afford a full outage for EU users.
[02:34] Carlos Ortiz: automatic routing/fallback to the nearest compatible model variant in another region as a temporary measure, and we can configure canary rollouts. we also support latency SLO-based routing so lower-tier requests can go to hosted if needed.
[02:50] Jordan Beck: pricing — we ran your cost calc and want to see committed tiers. we're aiming for a 20% headroom plus a reserved burst for peak season.
[02:59] Maya Patel: we'll send an updated pricing worksheet with three tiers: hosted increment, dedicated baseline with burst, and private (VPC+KMS) premium. includes token rates and a committed monthly reservation.
[03:14] Priya Singh: timeline-wise we need to have contract amendment signed before Feb payroll cycle to secure budget. can you commit to a draft by 2026-01-21?
[03:24] Maya Patel: yes we'll prepare a draft amendment. goal: sign-off by 2026-01-28 per your ask.
[03:32] Carlos Ortiz: for the benchmark we'll need your representative prompt set and a test harness — Jordan can you share the exact workload? we'll run it for 48 hours in eu-west-az and provide token-level latency/cost breakdowns.
[03:47] Jordan Beck: yes I'll share the CSV and a small runner script. aim to have that to you by 2026-01-16.
[03:56] Priya Singh: small note — we saw tokenization differences across model variants, sometimes counts differ by ~5% which affects cost. can you include tokenization mapping in the report?
[04:06] Carlos Ortiz: good point — we'll include tokenization deltas and per-token cost.
[04:12] Liam O'Neill: security question — how are audit logs surfaced for private deployments? we need long retention for regulatory audits.
[04:21] Nora Kim: private has optional long term audit retention and can export to your SIEM via S3 or secure streaming. encryption in transit and at rest, and we support your HSM-backed KMS for keys.
[04:34] Jordan Beck: cool. one small hiccup — procurement wants a vendor risk questionnaire answered. can you share your vendor pack and a primary contact?
[04:44] Maya Patel: I'll share the pack, Nora will be the point for security Qs.
[04:49] Nora Kim: yes I'll handle the VRQ — target turnaround 3 business days after you send it.
[04:56] Maya Patel: ok to recap next steps verbally?
[05:00] Jordan Beck: please.
[05:02] Maya Patel: action items: Carlos to run 48-hour benchmark in eu-west-az with your prompt set; Jordan to share prompt CSV + harness by 2026-01-16; Maya to draft contract amendment and pricing by 2026-01-21; Nora to share SOC2, network diagram, and handle VRQ.
[05:22] Priya Singh: timeline sounds good. also can you flag the dedicated pool sizing recommendation? we want guidance on pre-warming and cache strategy.
[05:31] Carlos Ortiz: we'll include recommended pool sizes, prewarm steps and KV/prefix cache suggestions based on your traffic distribution, and quantization profile impact.
[05:42] Liam O'Neill: one last item — are there any competitor lock-ins we should watch for?
[05:46] Maya Patel: none enforced. we support standard model versioning and exportable configs. competitors mentioned earlier are MegaCloud AI and AtlasServe doing similar regional offers.
[05:56] Jordan Beck: great. thanks everyone.
[06:00] Maya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with the worksheet and draft amendment.

End of transcript.

Recap & Next steps (in doc):
- Redwood: send updated pricing worksheet, draft amendment, SOC2+network diagrams, sample terraform for KMS.
- SE: run 48-hour eu-west-az benchmark and return latency/cost/tokenization report.
- SunForge: provide prompt sets, workload runner, confirm peak QPS numbers.
- Target dates: prompt set by 2026-01-16, benchmark results by 2026-01-20, draft amendment by 2026-01-21, sign-off target 2026-01-28.

Notes on transcription: some acronyms may be mis-heard (eu-west-az sometimes said as eu-west-one), and speaker overlap near minute marks.
